description: For ten years, Zeus and the Olympians fought Kronos and the Titans. The victory founded the order of the Greek world.

hero.hook: Ten years of cosmic war: children overthrow their fathers to found Olympus.

blocks.text: The **Titanomachy** is the primordial war of Greek mythology. For **ten years**, it pitted the **Titans**, the old divine generation, against the **Olympians** led by the young **Zeus**.
It's not just a family feud. It is the transition from a world of brute force to a world of order and law. The victory of Zeus fixes forever who reigns over the sky, the sea and the dead.

It all starts with **Kronos**, the youngest of the Titans. After dethroning his father Ouranos, he fears the same fate. He devours his children as soon as they are born. His wife **Rhéa** saves the last one: **Zeus**. She gives him a swaddled stone. The child grows up in secret in Crete.

blocks.caption: Titans versus Olympians: ten years to decide who reigns.

blocks.text: According to some versions, Zeus is fed by the goat **Amalthée**. While playing, he breaks one of his horns: it becomes the **cornucopia**, always full of food.

As an adult, Zeus forces Cronus to regurgitate **Hestia**, **Demeter**, **Hera**, **Hades** and **Poseidon**. The young gods settle on the **Olympus**. Kronos and the Titans hold Mount **Othrys**, in Thessaly. The war is getting bogged down. Other allies are needed.

Zeus frees from the **Tartar**, prison under the Underworld, the **Cyclops** and the **Hecatonchires**. The Cyclops, blacksmiths with a single eye, make the decisive weapons: the **lightning** for Zeus, the **trident** for Poseidon, an invisibility helmet for Hades.

The three Hecatonchires, Cottos, Briarée and Gygès, have a hundred arms and fifty heads. They tear off sections of mountain and throw them at the Titans. Beneath lightning and rocks, the old world crumbles. The defeated Titans are chained to Tartarus. Their jailers: the Hécatonchires, yesterday prisoners.

sections.title: Lightning, trident and a hundred arms

blocks.text: The winners draw lots. **Zeus** receives heaven and command. **Poseidon** receives the sea. **Hades** receives the underworld. The Olympian order replaces the cycle of parricide.

blocks.caption: Zeus, Poseidon and Hades: three brothers, three domains.

blocks.text: Some spared Titans retain a place in the new order. , guarantor of divine law, remains at the side of Zeus. [[Themis]]

Peace remains fragile. **Gaïa**, mother of the Titans, gives birth to more threats: the monster, then the [[Typhon]], war against the Giants. This time, the gods need a mortal, **Heracles**, to defeat. The era of heroes has begun. [[Gigantomachy (sequel to Titanomachy)]]

sections.title: Sharing the sky, the sea and the dead

blocks.text: The word “titanic” still recalls their strength. In 1795, the chemist  named **titanium** after them, for its resistance. The satellites of Saturn, planet of Cronus among the Romans, bear the names of Titans. [[Martin Heinrich Klaproth]]

The Titan **Atlas** remains famous for . Cartographers are inspired by it:  places his figure on collections of maps. The book itself is soon called a **atlas**. [[Atlas carrying the sky]] [[Mercator]]
The Olympians overthrow **Kronos** thanks to the Cyclops and the Hecatonchires. The Titans fall to Tartarus. Zeus, Poseidon and Hades share the world: the order of Olympus is born.
